text: Why is a syntax tree declared as a sealed interface with record implementations rather than as a class hierarchy?
choices: A class hierarchy could not express that `Bin` holds two sub-expressions of the same type.
Records are faster to allocate, which matters because a parser creates many nodes.
Sealed interfaces are the only Java construct that permits recursive type references.
It states that an expression is exactly one of a fixed set of shapes, so a `switch` over them needs no `default` and gains a new case as a compile error.
explanation: A syntax tree is the example algebraic data types were designed for: an expression is a number or a variable or a binary operation, and nothing else. The exhaustiveness check is the practical payoff — adding a `Call` node in Chapter 25 turns every tree walker into a compile error listing exactly what to update, which is the difference between a safe refactor and a search.
